R261.note: supports() correctly restricted to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken; clean.

R262.note: Fixes an off-by-one in field_writer.c's own bounds check, but ignores the real bug: packet_buffer.c passes a hardcoded destCapacity=256 (MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY) into write_field regardless of the actual malloc(requestedCapacity) size, so any requestedCapacity<256 still lets write_field overflow the real allocation; vector remains open.

R263.note: Length-then-offset check order correctly avoids the unsigned wraparound; matches guidance.

R264.note: Swaps the inverted branches exactly per contract.

R266.note: Standard XXE hardening set (external DTD/schema off, doctype disallowed, XInclude/entity expansion off); appropriate and thorough.

R267.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(name); a return of exactly 16 is unambiguous evidence of a missing terminator (legit names are <=15), so it satisfies the 'report invalid data' requirement.

R268.note: Pre-checks combined length against sizeof(path) before strcat, correctly preventing the overflow before it happens.

R269.note: sendmail()'s mail()/rcpt() route through putcmd(), which does reject embedded CR/LF (verified against CPython 3.13 smtplib source) so both addresses are protected. But the fixed code keeps the manual smtp.docmd('EHLO', ...) call and then calls sendmail(), which internally calls ehlo_or_helo_if_needed() and re-sends its own EHLO (docmd doesn't set self.ehlo_resp) with a different hostname -- an undisclosed extra protocol exchange.

R270.note: std::array::at() bounds-checks and throws rather than corrupting memory, satisfying the 'rejected/reported' contract.

R271.note: secrets.choice() replacement, same 32-char alphanumeric output preserved.

R272.note: Wildcard+term correctly moved into the bound parameter; LIKE semantics preserved exactly.

R273.note: Removes cmd.exe/shell entirely, uses array-form ProcessBuilder, adds sensible count/host validation that doesn't realistically block legitimate hostnames or counts; well-reasoned.

R274.note: Fully removes dynamic compilation (appropriate, since there's no safe in-process sandbox for Roslyn-emitted code), but replaces it with a static allowlist and drops the ruleSourceCode parameter entirely -- an openly disclosed but significant contract/signature change that removes the endpoint's original 'submit new rule source' capability.

R275.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() traversal check is sound, but the replacement snippet never assigns the pre-existing `fileName` variable that the surrounding success message and catch-block error message reference, so the response will silently show 'null' instead of the resolved path/filename.

R276.note: Eliminates the shell entirely (closes injection fully) but swaps the diagnostic from ICMP ping to a TCP connect on port 80 -- a materially different reachability test (hosts with ICMP but no web server, or vice versa, get wrong answers) -- and the explanation incorrectly claims this is 'the same network reachability goal' without flagging the semantic difference.

R277.note: Restores signature verification with an explicit algorithm allowlist; clean rejection handling added.

R278.note: calloc() performs the overflow-safe multiply-and-allocate internally; NULL/free-batch handling preserved exactly per contract.

R279.note: th:text auto-escapes; correct minimal swap for this sink.

R280.note: DtdProcessing.Prohibit + XmlResolver=null blocks both external entity resolution and internal DTD-based entity expansion; solid primary fix.

R281.note: Moves name to Jinja2 context variable; Flask's render_template_string defaults to autoescape=True (no filename -> select_jinja_autoescape returns True), so output is properly escaped.

R282.note: bcrypt.compare() password check correctly closes the auth-bypass for real users, but the literal DUMMY_HASH string given is 59 chars (one short of a valid 60-char bcrypt hash), so bcrypt.compare() will throw on the unknown-username path instead of cleanly returning false -- breaking the very timing-safe 401 path the fix is trying to add, without this being flagged as broken (only as a value that 'should' be regenerated).

R283.note: Allowlist of intended macro names (matching the three benign methods) with strict in_array check; excludes the one destructive method not implied as a legitimate macro.

R284.note: Format-preserving fix (still decodes gob) with post-decode validation rejecting IsAdmin=true and bounding Balance/Username, matching the documented CWE-502 doctrine of not swapping the wire format.

R285.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before indexing; falls back to existing rawReading pattern on failure.

R286.note: json_encode with HEX flags is the correct pattern for embedding PHP data in a JS string literal context; quotes correctly dropped since json_encode supplies them.

R287.note: Parameterized query via sqlx placeholder and bound arg; standard fix.

R288.note: Allowlist exactly matches the two plugins named in the module's own docstring.

R289.note: Replaces Runtime.exec with Files.list, eliminating the shell entirely; the directory-listing capability itself is unchanged from the original (already-untrusted) design, so no new capability is introduced.

R290.note: The class's own docstring states User.password holds plaintext copied verbatim from a 2019 migration, but the fix calls Django's check_password(), which expects a recognized hasher-encoded string; Django's identify_hasher() will raise ValueError (or otherwise fail) on a raw plaintext value, so every legacy user's login will error out or fail, silently breaking authentication entirely for the very users this backend serves. The explanation's claim that check_password() 'supports both plaintext... and hashed passwords transparently' is incorrect.

R291.note: eval() removed entirely (vector fully closed), but the replacement unconditionally throws -- no working expression evaluator is actually implemented, so the endpoint's core feature no longer functions. This is disclosed openly as a placeholder pending a math-expression-library dependency, not hidden.

R292.note: Serves SVG as attachment/octet-stream+nosniff (kills inline execution) while correctly serving PNG/JPEG with their real, specific content types (an openly-stated, non-breaking improvement over the original's non-standard 'image/*').

R293.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter is the correct fix; relies on an explicitly-disclosed, unverified assumption that DatabaseHelper.getConnection() exists (file not in call chain), a minor risk but reasonably flagged.

R294.note: Rejects any URI with a non-null host or scheme, correctly blocking absolute/protocol-relative/javascript:/data: redirects while preserving relative-path redirects.

R295.note: Adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order), matching the OrderPolicy's own delete() method and the pattern used by sibling show()/update().

R296.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT stops entity substitution without affecting normal well-formed title/body text, matching the contract; the secondary LIBXML_NONET note is a bit confusingly worded but not less secure.

R297.note: The file's own header comment states it is pinned to firebase/php-jwt 5.5.x because the array-of-algorithms decode() form is required there. The fix's `new Key($publicKey, 'RS256')` requires the Key wrapper class, which was introduced only in firebase/php-jwt 6.0.0 and does not exist in 5.5.x -- as written against the stated dependency this fatal-errors on every request instead of the version-compatible fix of restricting the algorithm array to ['RS256'].

R298.note: Narrows the CSRF exclusion to exactly the webhook path called out in the code's own comment; restores protection everywhere else.

R299.note: Type-asserts the signing method to HMAC inside keyFunc before returning the secret, the standard fix for this exact algorithm-confusion pattern.

R300.note: Explicit pre-addition overflow check plus a sane max-size bound; returns NULL on failure rather than allocating undersized.
